abstract: Social media has become an important information source for crisis management and provides quick access to ongoing developments and critical information. However, classification models suffer from event-related biases and highly imbalanced label distributions which still poses a challenging task. To address these challenges, we propose a combination of entity-masked language modeling and hierarchical multi-label classification as a multi-task learning problem. We evaluate our method on tweets from the TREC-IS dataset and show an absolute performance gain w.r.t. F1-score of up to 10% for actionable information types. Moreover, we found that entity-masking reduces the effect of overfitting to in-domain events and enables improvements in cross-event generalization. Our source code is publicly available on GitHub.

bibliographic.title: Enhancing Crisis-Related Tweet Classification with Entity-Masked Language Modeling and Multi-Task Learning
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the Second Workshop on NLP for Positive Impact (NLP4PI)

content.problem: Crisis tweet classifiers overfit to event-specific entities and biases and face highly imbalanced labels, so they perform poorly on rare actionable information types for unseen disaster events.
content.proposed_solution: The authors combine adaptive pre-training with entity-masked language modeling and hierarchical multi-label classification heads trained as a multi-task problem on top of BERT.
content.algorithm_or_model: Entity-masked language modeling (E-MLM) with hierarchical multi-task classification heads (HMCN) on BERT

metrics.name: AIT F1
metrics.condition: Best proposed model with E-MLM pre-training and hierarchical multi-task head, macro-averaged over actionable information types, TREC-IS 2020B test events

metrics.name: LB F1
metrics.condition: Best proposed model, macro-averaged over lower-level information types, TREC-IS 2020B test events

metrics.name: LT F1
metrics.condition: Best proposed model, macro-averaged over upper-level information types, TREC-IS 2020B test events

metrics.name: strict F1
metrics.condition: Entity extraction quality of the Google Cloud Natural Language API measured on 300 manually annotated tweets

metrics.name: absolute F1 gain
metrics.condition: Actionable information types, proposed approach versus baselines as reported for the TREC-IS evaluation

content.claim: The combination of entity-masked pre-training and hierarchical multi-task learning raises actionable information type F1 by up to 10 percent and improves generalization to unseen crisis events.
author_stated_limitations: The HMCNlocal model improves detection of rare actionable information types but lowers performance on the category containing the most information types.
Training with entity tokens could be task-specific and errors from named entity recognition systems can propagate into the model.

evidence.problem_quote: However, event-related biases and entities as shown in Figure 1 prevent models from generalizing to unseen disaster events and therefore degrade w.r.t. detection performance.

Moreover, we found that entity-masking reduces the effect of overfitting to in-domain events and enables improvements in cross-event generalization.
author_stated_limitation_quotes: As depicted in Figure 3, the HMCNlocal model improves the detection of rare actionable information types over the single-task model while at the same time decreasing the performance on the category with the most information types.
However, model training with such entities could be task-specific and prone to error propagation by named entity recognition systems.
